City stays planned until Jim wires testers and Mark's QA confirms schedule-only boards (no real-time) are an accepted product state. Modes v1: Metro Azul/Amarela/Verde/Vermelha only (56 line ticks / 50 unique stations after dedupe — see stats). OUT: CP urban commuter rail (Cascais, Sintra, Sul, Azambuja lines); Carris historic tram; Transtejo ferries; Carris Metropolitana / TUL bus.
Timezone Europe/Lisbon HAS DST (WET/UTC+0 standard, WEST/UTC+1 late Mar-late Oct). Do not copy Perth/Brisbane/Adelaide no-DST.

Four printed lines on the official diagram: Azul Reboleira - Santa Apolónia (18 stops), Amarela Odivelas - Rato (13 stops), Verde Telheiras - Cais do Sodré (13 stops), Vermelha S. Sebastião - Aeroporto (12 stops). 56 line ticks total. 50 unique open metro stations after dedupe (6 stations are each shared by exactly two lines - see interchanges). This corrects the oracle report's approximate 'Total: 56 unique' figure (marked '(approximate; exact dedupe at D1)' in the report) - the exact hand-transcribed unique count is 50, since Marquês de Pombal, Campo Grande, Saldanha, Baixa-Chiado, S. Sebastião, and Alameda each appear on two lines' printed stop lists.

Hub-lock (reference point, NOT a direction token): Marquês de Pombal (Azul x Amarela). Chosen over Alameda (Verde x Vermelha) per the direction-model memo: more central (Praça do Marquês de Pombal, top of Avenida da Liberdade), richest icon row on the diagram (bus, customer-care, wheelchair, bike, police - the only station with all five).

doNotGroup: the six interchange stations (Marquês de Pombal, Campo Grande, Saldanha, Baixa-Chiado, S. Sebastião, Alameda) are each shared by exactly two lines; no station on the official diagram is shared by three or four lines (unlike Brussels' Arts-Loi/Kunst-Wet). doNotGroup Roma vs Areeiro vs 'Roma/Areeiro' (the latter is a CP interchange pedestrian-link node, not a Metro stop - not inserted into stations[]).

CORRECTION TO ORACLE REPORT: the report's board-eligibility table lists 'Alcântara Terra (M Vermelha): + CP Linha do Sul' as an overlapping station. The official Aug 2026 network diagram does NOT show Alcântara-Terra or Alcântara-Mar on any Metro line - both print only on the CP-only beige corridor near Belém/Santos, nowhere near the Vermelha line's actual route (S. Sebastião to Aeroporto). Not inserted into stations[]. Flagged for Nico/Jim to confirm rather than silently guessed either way.

coverageGaps: CP urban commuter rail (Linha de Cascais, Linha de Sintra, Linha do Sul, Linha de Azambuja) - separate operator, separate boarding contract. Shares six stations with Metro (Oriente, Santa Apolónia, Terreiro do Paço, Cais do Sodré, Reboleira, and a pedestrian link near S. Sebastião) - all out of v1.
Carris historic tram network (Tram 12, 15, 18, 24, 25, 28, etc.) - separate operator, no GTFS-RT, out of v1.
Transtejo/Soflusa river ferries - out of v1 (mode exclusion); shown only as a beige/blue overlay on the official diagram for river-crossing context.
Carris Metropolitana / TUL bus - out of v1 (mode exclusion).

Alcântara-Terra / Alcântara-Mar - CP-only stations on the western Cascais/Sintra corridor near Belém/Santos; NOT on any Metro line per the official diagram. See notes for the oracle-report correction.
Roma/Areeiro CP interchange node - pedestrian link between Metro's Roma and Areeiro stops and the CP Roma-Areeiro railway station; not itself a Metro stop.
No 'Linha Circular' or other planned/under-construction line on this diagram edition - v1 is the four operating lines only.
